review.assessment: The diff introduces four standalone modules (`charges.py`, `retry.py`, `sla.py`, `summary.py`) that implement billing, retry scheduling, SLA evaluation, and summary statistics respectively. None of them correctly account for the newly added `cancelled` status, leaving active decision paths to treat cancelled jobs as unfinished or eligible for further processing. As a result, cancelled work will incorrectly keep its SLA timer running, incur charges, land in an undocumented 'other' bucket, and remain candidates for automatic retries.

findings.actual: It falls through to `return now`, causing the SLA calculation to use a moving target instead of the cancellation time. Cancelled jobs will show continuously worsening margins and false breaches.
findings.call: python3 -c "from jobs.sla import finished_at; from types import SimpleNamespace; j = SimpleNamespace(status='cancelled', ended_at=100); print(finished_at(j, now=500))"
findings.defect: `sla.py` does not treat cancelled jobs as finished
findings.expected: The function should recognize `CANCELLED` as a terminal state and return `job.ended_at`, stopping the SLA clock.

findings.actual: `is_chargeable` returns `True` when `cpu_seconds > 0`, even if the job was cancelled by the system. Cancelled jobs will be billed incorrectly.
findings.call: python3 -c "from jobs.charges import is_chargeable; from types import SimpleNamespace; j = SimpleNamespace(status='cancelled', cpu_seconds=10); print(is_chargeable(j))"
findings.expected: Billing should be voided for any job that was cancelled, matching the `FAILED` exclusion already present.

findings.actual: Cancelled jobs are silently grouped into `'other'`, making them invisible to dashboard queries and violating the spec that every status must have its own bucket.
findings.call: python3 -c "from jobs.summary import counts; from types import SimpleNamespace; j = SimpleNamespace(status='cancelled'); print(counts([j]))"
findings.defect: `summary.py` lacks a dedicated bucket for cancelled status
findings.expected: A `'cancelled'` entry must be added to `BUCKETS` and handled in the `counts` logic so it is tracked separately.

findings.actual: `should_retry` only excludes `DONE`. A cancelled job with retries left passes through and gets requeued.
findings.call: python3 -c "from jobs.retry import should_retry; from types import SimpleNamespace; j = SimpleNamespace(status='cancelled', attempts=0, kind='render'); print(should_retry(j))"
findings.expected: The scheduler must immediately reject any job with a `CANCELLED` status, as work was explicitly halted.
